title: Assessment of the Genotoxic Effects of Nanomaterials on Plant Tissues, Using Allium cepa as the Experimental Model Organism
content: Fertilizers enhance plant growth with lower toxicity than pesticides. Disruptions in the cell cycle, especially during mitosis, can cause cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, measured by the mitotic index (MI), which indicates the percentage of cells in each mitotic phase. Changes in MI are key indicators of environmental pollution from toxic substances [1,2]. Testing systems using plants like Allium cepa, Vicia faba, and Hordeum vulgare assess genotoxic agents in air, water, and soil, particularly for human risk evaluations and pesticide analysis. Allium cepa's apical meristem cells are effective for studying cellular effects, as substances with antimitotic and genotoxic properties can disrupt normal development and cause chromosomal damage, affecting apoptosis during cell division [3,4].
